title: Diagnosis of pregnancy, gestational dating, antenatal care schedule and routine screening

steps.say: Transvaginal ultrasound reliably detects early gestational structures before transabdominal scanning. The gestational sac becomes visible at 4.5 to 5 weeks with a mean diameter of 2 to 3 millimeters. By 5.5 weeks, the yolk sac appears consistently once mean sac diameter reaches 8 to 10 millimeters.
steps.tx: Early pregnancy confirmation utilizes **transvaginal sonography**, which detects the **gestational sac** at 4.5 to 5 weeks when the mean sac diameter measures 2 to 3 mm. The **yolk sac** becomes reliably visible at 5.5 weeks once the mean sac diameter reaches 8 to 10 mm.

steps.say: Accurate gestational age assignment is vital for every pregnancy decision. Crown-rump length measured between 7 and 13 weeks 6 days provides the most reliable dating ultrasound method, carrying a narrow error margin of plus or minus 5 to 7 days.
steps.tx: First-trimester **dating ultrasound** measuring embryonic **crown-rump length** between 7 and 13 weeks 6 days offers the highest precision for establishing **gestational age**, with an accepted clinical margin of error of plus or minus 5 to 7 days, superseding unreliable menstrual dating and ensuring precise timing for all subsequent screening and delivery decisions.

steps.say: Sonographic viability guidelines prevent premature intervention in developing embryos. A definite fetal heart pulsation must be demonstrated on transvaginal examination when the crown-rump length reaches 7 millimeters or greater. The absence of cardiac motion at this threshold defines non-viable pregnancy.
steps.tx: Definite embryonic viability mandates identifying active **fetal heart pulsation** once the **crown-rump length** measures 7 mm or more on high-resolution transvaginal sonography. Absence of visible embryonic cardiac motion at or beyond the 7 mm threshold confirms a definitive diagnosis of early **non-viable pregnancy** requiring clinical intervention.

steps.say: Nutritional preparation protects against severe developmental anomalies. Daily periconceptional folic acid at 400 micrograms prevents approximately 70 percent of neural tube defects. Women at high risk require higher dosages of 4 to 5 milligrams daily starting one month before conception.
steps.tx: Routine **periconceptional** supplementation with **folic acid** at 400 micrograms daily prevents over 70 percent of **neural tube defects** including anencephaly and spina bifida. High-risk mothers with previous affected offspring, pregestational diabetes, or on anti-epileptic therapy require higher therapeutic dosing of 4 to 5 mg daily starting 1 month before conception.

left.title: Standard Risk Supplementation
points: Prevents 70 percent of neural tube defects

right.title: High Risk Supplementation
points: Prior NTD, pregestational diabetes, valproate use
Begin at least 1 month before planned conception

steps.say: The World Health Organization transformed antenatal scheduling to improve maternal survival. The comprehensive 2016 model replaces older four-visit models with a minimum of 8 antenatal contacts. The initial visit occurs before 12 weeks, followed by visits across mid and late pregnancy.
steps.tx: The **WHO model** establishes a schedule of at least 8 **antenatal contacts** to reduce perinatal mortality. The **first contact** takes place before 12 weeks, with subsequent visits arranged at 20, 26, 30, 34, 36, 38, and 40 weeks of gestation.

nodes.label: First contact: < 12 weeks booking and baseline labs
Third and fourth contacts: 26 and 30 weeks glucose and Rh
Late pregnancy contacts: 34, 36, 38 and 40 weeks delivery planning

steps.say: Screening for carbohydrate intolerance occurs universally during late second trimester. Between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation, clinicians perform gestational diabetes screening using a standard 75 gram oral glucose tolerance test or the DIPSI non-fasting single-step procedure.
steps.tx: Universal **gestational diabetes screening** is scheduled between 24 and 28 weeks of gestation using a 75 g **oral glucose tolerance test** or single-step **DIPSI** non-fasting protocol, identifying impaired maternal insulin resistance before third-trimester fetal macrosomia, polyhydramnios, and neonatal metabolic complications accelerate.

right.title: DIPSI Single-Step Protocol
points: Non-fasting 75 g oral glucose load administered

steps.say: Neonatal early-onset sepsis prevention targets maternal genital colonisation. Universal culture screening for Group B Streptococcus occurs between 36 and 37 weeks 6 days using combined recto-vaginal swabs, determining the need for intrapartum penicillin G prophylaxis during labour.
steps.tx: Universal culture screening for **Group B Streptococcus** is performed between 36 and 37 weeks 6 days of gestation using combined recto-vaginal swabs. Identified maternal colonization guides targeted **intrapartum prophylaxis** with intravenous **penicillin G** initiated immediately upon rupture of membranes or onset of active labour to prevent early-onset neonatal sepsis.

rows: Ampicillin: 2 g loading then 1 g q4h
Cefazolin: 2 g loading then 1 g q8h

steps.say: Alloimmunisation prophylaxis protects future Rh-negative pregnancies from severe hemolytic disease. Unsensitized mothers receive 300 micrograms of anti-D immunoglobulin at 28 weeks gestation, followed by a second dose within 72 hours of delivering an Rh-positive infant.
steps.tx: To prevent maternal red cell **isoimmunisation**, prophylactic **anti-D immunoglobulin** (300 micrograms or 1500 IU) is administered routinely at 28 weeks of gestation to non-sensitized **Rh-negative** women, with repeat dosing provided within 72 hours following the birth of a confirmed Rh-positive infant or following any invasive prenatal procedure.
